title: Mince and Onion Pie
subtitle: A shortcrust beef pie with soft onions and rich gravy
excerpt: Minced beef and soft onions in a thick, savoury gravy, encased in shortcrust pastry. A proper weeknight pie that fills the kitchen with good smells.
sourceNotes: Adapted from British home-cooking tradition for a standard 23cm shortcrust pie.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead. Keep it chilled and assemble the pie when needed.

content.text: This is a straightforward minced beef pie with a proper shortcrust lid and base. Cook the mince until the gravy is thick before it goes into the pastry. A runny filling makes a soggy base.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Remove and set aside.
Turn the heat to high. Add the mince and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned all over. Drain off any excess fat.
Return the onion to the pan. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and worcestershire sauce.
Pour in the beef stock. Stir well and simmer for 15 minutes until the gravy is thick. Season with salt and pepper. Leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a little overhang.
Spoon the cold filling into the case. Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg and press the lid on firmly. Trim and crimp the edges.
Cut two small slits in the top. Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 35 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.cause: The filling went in warm, so the pastry steamed from the inside.
items.fix: Cool the filling fully before it touches the pastry. Bake on a preheated baking sheet for extra crispness.

items.symptom: The pastry lid breaks apart when cut.
items.cause: The pastry was rolled too thin or the filling was still hot when it went in.
items.fix: Roll the lid to at least 3mm thick and always use a cold filling.

items.cause: The gravy was not reduced enough before the pie was assembled.
items.fix: Simmer the filling for an extra 10 minutes with the lid off until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
